p.SYNC-FROM-CODE-IS-AN-EXCEPTIONAL-PROTOCO: Sync-from-Code is an exceptional protocol, not a default.

p.this-document-is-the-decision-table: This document is the decision table for *should I run it right now?*

p.RUN-WHEN-A-DIRECT-EDIT-TOUCHES-WHAT-THE-: You (the human) opened a source file and changed a value, a constant, or a piece of logic that the spec pins.

p.THE-EDIT-IS-DELIBERATE-AND-PERMANENT: The edit is deliberate and permanent — you plan to keep it.

p.example-direct-edit: *Example:* adjusted `TIMEOUT = 600` in `src/verify.rs`. Spec still says 300 s.

p.RUN-WHEN-AN-IMPERATIVE-CHAT-COMMAND-CHAN: You told the agent "change the timeout to 600 s" or "switch the hash function to blake3" without updating the spec first.

p.THE-AGENT-EXECUTED-AND-THE-CODE-REFLECTS: The agent executed and the code now reflects the new choice.

p.example-imperative-chat-command: *Example:* session transcript shows the user asked the agent to replace `SHA256::digest` calls with `blake3::hash`. PROP-000 still specifies SHA-256.

p.RUN-WHEN-AN-EXPERIMENT-CONVERGED: You were trying two candidates; one won.

p.THE-SPEC-STILL-DESCRIBES-THE-EXPERIMENT-: The spec still describes the experiment-in-progress state, or still names the loser as the current answer.

p.example-experiment-converged: *Example:* tried both fixed and adaptive timeout; fixed-600 s won on measured data. Code is fixed-600 s. Spec still says "adaptive, TBD".

skip-temp.title: The code change is temporary

p.SKIP-DEBUG-SCAFFOLDING-PROBES-AND-SHORT-: Debug scaffolding, ad-hoc probes, a reproducer you plan to delete within the day.

p.DO-NOT-DIGNIFY-A-TEMPORARY-CHANGE-WITH-A: Do not dignify it with a sync.

p.record-the-skip-in-the-wal-lead: Record the skip explicitly in the WAL so the next session does not try:

skip-temp.fence: ## Constraints - src/verify.rs: temporary trace logging for #42 reproduction, do NOT sync to spec.

p.THE-WAL-ENTRY-KEEPS-THE-NEXT-SESSION-HON: The WAL entry is what keeps the next session honest.

p.without-it-a-sync-happy-agent-promotes-t: Without it, a sync-happy agent will try to promote the trace logging to a first-class spec feature.

p.SKIP-FORMATTING-IMPORT-ORDER-DEAD-CODE-A: `cargo fmt`, import reorder, dead-code removal the compiler already flagged, rename of a private symbol that has no public contract.

p.THE-SPEC-LIVES-AT-A-HIGHER-LEVEL-OF-RESO: The spec lives at a higher level of resolution than these changes.

p.SYNC-WOULD-PRODUCE-NOISE-NOT-A-DECISION-: Sync would produce noise, not a decision record.

p.IF-THE-HONEST-ANSWER-IS-IT-FELT-BETTER-S: If the honest answer to "why did the code change?" is "it felt better" or "I don't remember", stop.

p.SYNC-IS-NOT-FOR-LAUNDERING-UNREASONED-DR: Sync-from-Code is not for laundering unreasoned drift into the spec. Two paths:

facts.PATH-RECOVER-THE-REASON: **Recover the reason.** Re-read the session, the measurements, the issue. If a durable reason exists, surface it and run the protocol normally.
facts.PATH-REVERT-THE-CODE: **Revert the code.** If no reason can be named, the code change itself is suspect. Revert.

p.DO-NOT-PRODUCE-A-SPEC-CHANGE-THAT-READS-: Do not produce a spec change that reads "we do X because we do X".

p.a-tautology-with-a-date-attached-is-not-: That is not a decision, it is a tautology with a date attached.

skip-bootstrap.title: The spec section does not exist yet

p.SKIP-WHEN-THE-CODE-IMPLEMENTS-SOMETHING-: The code implements something the spec does not mention at all.

p.SYNC-UPDATES-EXISTING-ENTRIES-IT-DOES-NO: Sync-from-Code is for **updating** existing spec entries, not for bootstrapping them.

p.a-brand-new-section-via-sync-is-a-classi: Putting a brand-new spec section together via Sync-from-Code produces "spec that matches the code that was written without a spec" — a classic retrofit, and everyone can tell.

flowchart.title: Quick decision flow
flowchart.fence: Did code change since last spec-aligned state? ─ no ─→ done │ yes ▼ Is the change temporary? ─ yes ─→ record in WAL, done │ no ▼ Is the change purely mechanical? ─ yes ─→ done (no sync) │ no ▼ Does the relevant spec section already exist? ─ no ─→ draft spec normally │ yes ▼ Can you name the reason in one sentence? ─ no ─→ recover or revert │ yes ▼ Run Sync-from-Code (SYNC-PROTOCOL.xml).

facts.BOUNDARY-FLOW-WAL: **`flow:wal`** handles session continuity. A successful sync may trigger a WAL update; that update goes through the WAL flow, not this one.
facts.BOUNDARY-FLOW-ATOMIC-COMMITS: **`flow:git-atomic-commits`** handles commit discipline: one sync, one commit, one logical idea. The message *format* — Conventional Commits, with `docs(spec)` as the type a sync commit carries — is defined by the sibling `flow:git-conventional-commits`, not by the atomicity flow and not here.
facts.BOUNDARY-VIBE-BUILD: **`vibe build`** (M1.5+) handles the other direction — generating code from spec. A sync can be followed by a build, but they are independent flows.
